newsitem.title: UK: European stocks mixed as dollar slips.
newsitem.headline: European stocks mixed as dollar slips.

text.p: Continental European share markets slipped on Thursday after Wall Street's three-day comeback came to an abrupt halt overnight, but London reversed its early losses.
On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar retreated from a 55-month high against the yen as traders became increasingly nervous about possible Japanese intervention.
The dollar also slipped against the mark although it recovered a little as German officials, conspicuously silent in the last few days, made positive comments about the dollar's recent surge.
New York dictated the trend on the continental share markets as the U.S. rally, which followed last week's 215-point tumble, reversed after European dealers went home on Wednesday.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed down 45.33 points, or 0.69 percent, at 6,563.84.
But the European losses were modest, falling short in percentage terms of the Wall Street drop. The German market was down 0.26 percent by early afternoon while the Paris bourse lost 0.31 percent.

London also took an early dip in line with Wall Street and a weaker futures market. But it recovered modestly, with the FTSE-100 index up 16.1 points, or 0.38 percent, at 4,308.4 points.by mid-session
Firmer futures and fading memories of Wall Street prompted the gains but they had little conviction.
"There's precious little selling and the buyers come and go," said one London dealer.

London investors had reasons of their own to sit on the fence. Campaigning for the May 1 general election, where the ruling Conservatives are struggling to narrow the Labour Party's big opinion poll lead, injected the usual dose of uncertainty.
Finance minister Kenneth Clarke was due to hold his last monthly meeting on monetary policy before the election with Bank of England Governor Eddie George at 1415 GMT.
Analysts believe an unpopular interest rate rise, which most believe is needed to nip inflation, would come after the polls rather than before, whoever wins.
"No one really expects an interest rate rise but no one can afford to be disinterested just in case," said one dealer.
Water stocks rose after press reports suggested that Labour's planned windfall tax on privatised utilities would be lower than some expected.
Labour's finance spokesman, Gordon Brown, said a decision on the size of the one-off tax would not be made until after the election.
Paris dealers had hoped that the Bank of France might trim interest rates on Thursday. But the central bank left rates unchanged and the market consolidated after Wednesday's gains.
The CAC-40 index was down 7.99 points, or 0.31 percent, at 2,609.56 by early afternoon.
Wall Street also pulled down the German market, with the DAX index down 8.88 points or 0.26 percent at 3,350.58. Dealers also blamed the weakening of the dollar against the mark.
German industry has benefited from the mark's weakness in recent months against the dollar and sterling, which has tracked the U.S. currency more than its European counterparts.

A major German exporter, carmaker Volkswagen, gave evidence of this on Thursday, saying the mark's weakening had boosted 1996 earnings by about 600 million marks ($350 million). It also expected 1997 profits to benefit.
The dollar slipped from its 55-month high overnight against the yen with dealers jittery about the possibility of Bank of Japan intervention.

It was at 125.78 yen compared with the high of 127.16 and Wednesday's European close of 126.83. It also edged down from a 37-month high of 1.7272 marks to 1.7157 compared with the previous close of 1.7250.
As European markets opened, Japanese officials expressed concern about the dollar's rise against the yen in stronger terms than in recent days.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said the yen's recent fall against the dollar was excessive, and that Japan would deal decisively and in a timely manner with excessive currency moves.

"The comments from the MOF (Ministry of Finance) are clearly drawing a line in the sand, which is unnerving simply because the dollar has risen so far so sharply," said Mark Hendriks, international economist at SBC Warburg here.
After its early slide, the dollar was lifted by supportive comments by German officials.

Bundesbank Council member Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher said: "We do not need to strengthen the mark." The state secretary at the German finance ministry, Juergen Stark, also said a dollar/mark exchange rate over 1.72 was part of a normal market correction.
CURRENCIES AT 1120 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7157 marks and 125.78 yen, compared with 1.7250 and 126.83 in late European trade on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1120 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 16.1 points at 4,308.4.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 8.88 points
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was 7.99 points lower at 2,609.56.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1120 GMT
Gold was fixed in the morning at $348.05 compared with the London close of $347.95 on Wednesday. Silver was down two cents at $4.77.
